correctness.rationale: Exact log ratio divided by initial x has g(x)=(b-a)+aR2 e^{-bx}-bR1 e^{-ax}. Its derivative changes sign at most once and has an interior strict minimum iff R2>R1. Endpoint and exact minimum yield the necessary/sufficient open inequalities, and show at most two positive roots for all parameters. Strict convexity of u^(b/a) proves common-K rigidity. Taylor expansion with exact gmin and gxx proves sqrt onset, and quadratic substitution proves the exact witness. Verified arithmetic checker exercises critical formulas; finite tests are not the proof.

value.rationale: Provides a complete nontrivial phase boundary for a motivated population recruitment question (which of two seasonal environments should occur first), including a two-switch parameter wedge, rigid zero-switch behavior at equal positive carrying capacity and quantitative sqrt opening of order reversals. This links crowding contrast and low-density reproduction to order sensitivity without claiming asymptotic dynamics. The open interval is mathematically nonempty for every R1>1; results cannot be inferred from finite samples or monotone Beverton-Holt recruitment. Results are specific and structural rather than a selected numerical slice.
